title: Most Popular NBA Cards: Wemby, Curry & Courtyard.io’s Marketplace Data
body_markdown:
Since 1946,[the NBA](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=basketball) has seen plenty of legends come and go. There’s the Ice Man ([George Gervin](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=George%20Gervin&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ), Magic ([Earvin Johnson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Magic%20Johnson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ), His Airness ([Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ), The Answer ([Allen Iverson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Allen%20Iverson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ), the Black Mamba ([Kobe Bryant](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kobe%20Bryant&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ), and an ongoing debate about quite a few GOATs. However, more recently, the conversation has shifted to players that have earned the right to be named after a mythical creature: the unicorn.


Back in 2016[Kevin Durant](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kevin%20Durant&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) gave then-rookie[Kristaps Porzingis](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kristaps%20Porzingis&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) the nickname due to his mix of size (7’2”), three-point shooting, and handles. Today, Wemby is the closest example of a unicorn, and[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) ’s data shows that collectors can’t get enough of the enigmatic big man.


With the 2026-27 NBA season in full swing,[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) took a look who collectors have chased thus far, from Wembanyama to the ageless[Stephen Curry](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Stephen%20Curry&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)


In the first 12 days of November alone, thousands of basketball searches were logged on[Courtyard.io’s marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bpage%5D=2) , headlined by a monster peer-to-peer sale for a $24,495 Stephen Curry Kaboom! and surging demand for second-year phenom Victor Wembanyama.


For those looking to add The Alien and Chef Curry to their collection, Courtyard.io’s got a[Limited Drop](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=limited_drop) full of unicorns and all-time greats:[the Basketball Cup: Unicorn Night Pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=limited_drop) which is available now. For everyone else, the 2026-27 NBA season is just heating up.


Time for tip-off!


## **Victor Wembanyama and Stephen Curry Rewrite the Definition of a NBA Unicorn**


What started as a nickname for Porzingis has since spread throughout the league.


From The Process ([Joel Embiid](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Joel%20Embiid&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ), to The Joker ([Nikola Jokic](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Nikola%20Jokic&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ), the league’s tallest players now look more like point guards, chucking threes, dropping defenders, and taking the ball up the court in a way that was simply unimaginable a little over a decade ago. However, as *The Ringer* pointed out, “[If everyone is a unicorn, no one is.](https://www.theringer.com/2019/10/07/nba/year-of-the-unicorn-nba) ”


That’s why we’re proposing a new definition for the NBA’s unicorns—one that’s on-brand for collectors: one-of-ones.


Let’s start with the Alien,[Victor Wembanyama](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Victor%20Wembanyama&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) . Sure, he doesn’t have Embiid’s MVP trophy—or Jokic’s ring—but Wemby’s slender build is more akin to Kevin Durant than either of the somewhat more traditional-looking centers, and the league has never seen anything like the 7’4” Frenchman.


Taking this a step further, we’re going to share a hot take: unicorns don’t *have* to be bigs. Instead, they’re more like a one-of-one pull from a pack: a player that simply can’t be replicated…and who better than the one and only[Steph Curry](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Stephen%20Curry&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , arguably the greatest shooter of all time, the NBA’s record holder for most three-pointers made, to take that title.


It just so happens that the NBA Cup sees Curry’s Golden State Warriors and Wembanyama’s San Antonio Spurs face off against each other—and Courtyard has the packs (and the data) to help collectors prepare.


## **The Priciest Victor Wembanyama, Stephen Curry, and Dylan Harper Sales on Courtyard:**


As the Warriors and Spurs prepare for their NBA Cup matchup,[crazy court design](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/50174098/2026-nba-cup-tournament-court-designs) and all, here are the top peer-to-peer sales on the Courtyard.io’s marketplace for the game’s top stars:


- [Stephen Curry](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Stephen%20Curry&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) – 2019 Panini Crown Royale Kaboom! #19 (PSA 10 GEM MINT) – FMV: $24,495, sold on November 9th, 2026
- [Victor Wembanyama](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Victor%20Wembanyama&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) – 2022 Bowman Chrome University #101 Prospect Autograph (PSA 10 GEM MINT) – FMV: $7,000, sold on[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) ’s marketplace on July 12th, 2026
- [Dylan Harper](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Dylan%20Harper&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) – 2025 Topps Chrome Autograph Issue Rookies #TAIR-DH Green Refractor (PSA 10 GEM MINT) – FMV: $3,000 sold Sep. 6th, 2026


Curry's Kaboom! leads the board, even though it’s the only non-rookie-card on the list. In fact, Curry’s Kaboom! is the second-highest peer-to-peer sale of a basketball card on[Courtyard.io’s marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bpage%5D=2) —missing the top spot by just $505 (trailing only a 1984 Star #101 Michael Jordan at $25,000)—and stands as the highest ultra-modern sports card sale ever on the platform.


Making both deals sweeter still,[sellers on Courtyard.io’s marketplace pay $0 in seller fees](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/is-courtyard-io-legit-heres-what-you-need-to-know) . Yes, you read that right: Sellers on[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) ’s marketplace pay 0% seller fees, which saved these sellers thousands in seller fees compared to other marketplaces.


Sometimes, it’s worth zigging while others zag, especially when it comes to future Hall of Famers. But sales are only one side of the story. That’s why we decided to take a look into the players collectors are searching for, too.


## **Wembanyama Cards Rank Sixth in**[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) **’s Early Season NBA Searches:**


The 2026-27 NBA season is less than a month old, but collectors have been clamoring for cardboard featuring a mix of today’s superstars and the best players of yesterday.


For example, while Victor Wembanyama recently set a new career high with 52 points (to go along with 24 rebounds and 8 blocks) against the Dallas Mavericks, he ranks *just* outside of the top-five most-searched NBA players on[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) since the start of November.


### **Here are the five players that outranked Wemby to make**[Courtyard.io](http://courtyard.io/) **’s list of the most-searched NBA players in November.**


1. [Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)
2. [Kobe Bryant](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kobe%20Bryant&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)
3. [LeBron James](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=LeBron%20James&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)
4. [Cooper Flagg](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cooper%20Flagg&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)
5. [Luka Dončić](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Luka%20Doncic&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)


A trio of GOATs own the top three spots, but youngsters like Flagg and Doncic clearly have next—especially considering[Doncic’s lights out start to the season](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7777013/2026/11/13/lakers-luka-doncic-title-contenders-rountable/) .


## **Why Courtyard Is the Place to Chase Basketball Cards:**


Every card on Courtyard is[slabbed, graded and authenticated](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/welcome-to-card-school-the-difference-between-slabbed-cards-and-their-raw-counterparts) , so you know exactly what you're chasing, from a Kaboom! Curry to a Wemby prospect auto.


If you'd rather go unicorn hunting in a pack, the[Basketball Cup: Unicorn Night](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/basketball-cup-tournament-3) features chase cards from players in Friday’s Warriors vs. Spurs game (Stephen Curry, Victor Wembanyama, Dylan Harper,[De’Aaron Fox](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=De%27Aaron%20Fox&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and[Jimmy Butler](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Jimmy%20Butler&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ), costs $49 and runs from Friday, November 13th through Monday morning, November 16th.

- [Dylan Harper](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Dylan%20Harper&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) – 2025 Topps Signature Class Rookie Class Autographs #RCA-DH (PSA 9 MINT) – FMV: $472
